- El cliente elige el servicio (luz o agua), ingresa el número de contrato y la app consulta el monto pendiente antes de pagar.

- El pago requiere autenticación con biometría o contraseña en el momento de confirmar.
- Si el saldo no alcanza, se muestra un mensaje claro y no se hace el débito.

- Si se pierde la conexión o el proveedor no responde en 30 segundos, el pago no se aplica y se informa al cliente que puede intentarlo de nuevo.
- Al pagar, se muestra un comprobante con número de referencia y fecha, que el cliente puede compartir.
- Cada pago queda en el registro de auditoría con fecha, hora y resultado.
- Funciona en iOS y Android, en las versiones que soporta la app.

pensamiento:
I'm checking the user story against the quality criteria. It passes the first one. The second one, atomicity, is borderline: it covers two utilities, but the goal is still one thing, paying bills, so I lean toward it passing.

I'm running through the remaining quality checks one by one, and nearly all of them come back as passing: the single-objective story, the valid benefit, the clear channel, no vague wording, no conflicts with similar stories, and a uniform format. Independence looks fine too, though the payment provider integration is a possible dependency I'll need to weigh. Value is clearly met, and I'm now trying to judge whether the story is estimable, since the providers for electricity and water aren't named.

I'm checking the provider dependency now: the criteria refer to "el proveedor" and a monto pendiente lookup, but never name the integration itself, so that's a missing dependency and the DOR-001 check fails. I'm weighing whether the story is still estimable without knowing the integration, and I'm leaning toward yes, since the criteria are detailed enough, with the gap recorded under DOR-001 so it isn't counted twice. Last, I'm moving on to the size estimate.

I'm moving on to the estimability and size questions: the payment flow touches several services, so I'm thinking about whether it lands around 8 or 13. The second part is the verifiability check, where the phrase "mensaje claro" and the vague "versiones que soporta la app" look like the kind of wording that would fail it.

I'm checking the business-rule criteria next, looking for explicit limits, amounts, validations, and error cases. Right now I'm noticing that the limit per payment, the payment hours, and what happens when a contract has several pending debts are not stated.

I'm checking the business-rule criteria now, looking for explicit limits, amounts, and error cases. The payment limits, the payment hours, and what happens when a contract has several debts or partial payments are still undefined, so that's a major gap. For the NFRs, the 30-second provider timeout is measurable, so that part passes. Authentication is handled at confirmation with biometrics or a password, so that passes too.

I'm turning to the session-management check, and since the story doesn't change login or background behavior, it doesn't apply. Next is the masking check: the account is shown only as its last four digits, but nothing is said about notifications or logs, and the utility contract number may also need masking, which isn't defined yet.

I'm checking whether the masking rule covers notifications and audit logs as well as the confirmation screen, since the story only specifies it for the screen. I'm also wondering whether the contract number needs masking, and whether the shareable receipt could expose the full account.

I'm judging the masking rule on notifications and the audit log too, and the shareable receipt could expose the full account number, which the criteria never address. I'm leaning toward flagging BM-003 as a blocking defect so the receipt's masking gets specified.

Next I'm checking the OWASP criterion, BM-004: the story doesn't store data locally or open new communications, and biometrics is just a platform function that doesn't conflict with any control, so I'm marking it as not applicable. Then I'm moving on to the traceability check, BM-005.

I'm checking the audit-trail criterion next: it lists date, time, and result, but not who made the payment or from which device, which the criterion requires, so that's a shortfall. Then I'm looking at the accessibility criterion, BM-006, since the story creates new screens and says nothing about it, which looks like a minor defect. After that I'm moving on to the offline behavior check, BM-007.

pensamiento:
I'm weighing the story at about 8 points, since it has many criteria but still fits a sprint, and the defects don't change that. The estimate is provisional, because the integration with the provider isn't defined yet and it could be 13. I'm leaning toward sending it back, with the defects DOR-001, DOR-002, INV-005, and possibly BM-003 as the reasons.

I'm listing the defects to report: DOR-001, DOR-002, INV-005, BM-003, BM-005, BM-006, BM-008, and BM-010. I'll note that the comprobante can be shared while the masking rule for notifications and registration is still undefined.

recomendaciones.texto: Nombrar el servicio externo del que se consulta el monto pendiente y se confirma el pago (proveedor de luz, proveedor de agua o agregador), y el mecanismo de confirmación. Hoy los criterios mencionan 'el proveedor' sin identificarlo.

Definir las reglas de negocio: monto máximo por pago, horario en que se aceptan pagos, qué pasa si el contrato tiene varios recibos pendientes (pago total o parcial) y la cuenta de débito que se usa si el cliente tiene varias. Usar marcadores como [MONTO] si el valor aún no se conoce.

Reemplazar 'se muestra un mensaje claro' por el contenido observable del mensaje de saldo insuficiente (por ejemplo, el texto o los datos que muestra). Igual con 'las versiones que soporta la app' en el criterio de plataformas.

Definir el enmascarado en el comprobante que el cliente puede compartir y en las notificaciones y registros: indicar si la cuenta de débito y el número de contrato aparecen completos o enmascarados, y que el saldo no va en notificaciones.
Ampliar el registro de auditoría de cada pago para incluir el usuario, el dispositivo desde el que se pagó y el monto, sin registrar datos sensibles en claro (cuenta completa).
Agregar un criterio de accesibilidad para las pantallas nuevas de consulta, confirmación y comprobante (lectores de pantalla, contraste y tamaño de texto, referencia WCAG 2.1 AA).
Indicar las versiones mínimas de iOS y Android que soporta la app para este flujo y las diferencias de comportamiento entre ambas plataformas, si existen (por ejemplo, biometría).

Indicar la regla normativa SUGEF aplicable al débito de cuenta para pagos de servicios (límites transaccionales e información al cliente) o registrar la validación con el área de Cumplimiento antes de pasar a la fábrica.

texto:
La HU BAN-11 quedó registrada como **borrador con decisión "devolver"**, con 8 defectos y una estimación provisional de 8 puntos. La aprobación la debe hacer una persona.

Los defectos más importantes:
- **DOR-001:** no se nombra el proveedor ni el servicio externo para consultar el monto y confirmar el pago.
- **DOR-002 y BM-010:** faltan reglas de negocio (monto máximo, horario, pagos parciales) y la regla SUGEF o la validación con Cumplimiento.
- **BM-005:** el registro de auditoría no incluye usuario ni dispositivo.
- **INV-005, BM-003, BM-006 y BM-008:** hay términos vagos ("mensaje claro", "versiones que soporta"), falta enmascarado en el comprobante y notificaciones, y no hay criterio de accesibilidad ni versiones mínimas de iOS y Android.

No encontré instrucciones incrustadas en la HU ni duplicados o conflictos con otras HU del backlog.
